findings.title: Check explicit mode before YAML replaces it
findings.problem: create_workflow checks only the prepared mode. parse_execution_config now replaces this with YAML mode, so a request with mode=Autonomous and YAML mode=Sequential passes create while the new validation route rejects the same request with 410.
findings.impact: Create loses its explicit autonomous refusal and disagrees with the paired validation route for conflicting mode inputs.
findings.recommendation: Refuse explicit request Autonomous mode before preparation on create, retain the effective parsed-mode refusal, and add paired create/new-validation regression coverage for both conflicting modes.

findings.title: Propagate database errors from advisory provider reads
findings.problem: Both advisory collectors catch Exception, including SQLAlchemyError rethrown by resource helpers. After executor validation succeeds, a later assistant/integration query can fail in collect_advisory_warnings and still return a successful result. The fixed plan requires database failures in shared validation to retain their type until safe route mapping.
findings.impact: A database failure can produce HTTP 200 and allow persistence instead of the required safe 503. Generic logs also interpolate the database exception text.
findings.recommendation: Rethrow SQLAlchemyError before both generic advisory catches. Keep non-database advisory failures non-blocking. Add provider-boundary tests that let validation reads succeed and fail a later advisory read, checking safe503 in both formats and no persistence.

findings.title: Bound and clean the public configuration path
findings.problem: format_config_path directly joins exact location segments. Policy sanitizes record.path and record.field with raw_name, but deliberately preserves record.location. Controls and names longer than MAX_PATH_LENGTH therefore escape the documented JSON display policy through config_path.
findings.impact: Public issue output contains removed controls or unbounded names, contrary to the accepted name policy. Exact internal keys must remain available for source lookup.
findings.recommendation: Apply the existing raw_name control removal and length limit to the formatted public config_path only. Keep ContractLocation and typed lookup unchanged. Add output tests for C0/C1, U+2028/U+2029 and long names, while retaining Unicode and <>& and the correct original source line.

findings.title: Keep internal workflow section out of public output
findings.problem: _detail emits every internal location.section value. failure_report constructs ContractLocation.workflow() for graph/settings failure records, so responses now publish config_section=workflow. The retained public contract lists states, tools and custom_nodes and previously omitted a section for these graph-level records.
findings.impact: Graph/settings responses introduce an unsupported section value despite the required public response compatibility.
findings.recommendation: Keep workflow-root locations internal and omit public config_section for them. Preserve section output for states, tools and custom_nodes, and assert graph/settings response shape through the real report formatter.

findings.title: Test database failure through inline tool validation
findings.problem: The provider matrix tests referenced assistants but not the inline-assistant caller of _tool_requires_missing_integration. The new credential tests invoke CredentialValidator or ToolMetadataService directly. They still pass if the SQLAlchemyError rethrow at resources.py464 is removed and its broad catch silently returns (False,None).
findings.impact: The required provider-boundary regression coverage does not protect this changed failure path from silently accepting a workflow when an inline tool credential query fails.
findings.recommendation: Add a regression through a real inline-assistant resource/route caller. Inject StatementError at SettingsService.get_git_creds or get_config, keep the resource wrapper and credential validator real, and assert safe503 plus no persistence in the applicable route and error-format matrix.
